records.notes: Fuel state: no fuel.

source.name: Vital MX: 2025 Honda CRF250R Works Edition vs Yamaha YZ250F

records.notes: 'With fluids' assumed to include fuel. The Honda figure is the Works Edition, not the standard CRF250R. No front/rear split published.

records.topic: how much a full tank weighs
records.statement: A full tank adds roughly 10-12 lb: 1.85 gal on the KTM-family bikes works out to about 11.3 lb, and 1.6 gal on the Japanese bikes to about 9.8 lb, which matches the 10-12 lb gap seen between empty and full weigh-ins.

source.name: BAK calculation from published tank volumes and Vital MX 2022 250 Shootout empty/full weights

records.notes: Pump gasoline about 6.1 lb/gal (0.73 kg/L). 1.85 x 6.1 = 11.3; 1.60 x 6.1 = 9.8; 1.69 x 6.1 = 10.3. Measured empty-to-full differences in the 2022 250 weigh-in: KTM 10, Husqvarna 10, GasGas 10, Honda 11, Kawasaki 12, Yamaha 12 lb. Use this to convert no-fuel weights to full-tank weights when comparing sources.

records.statement: KTM lists a 63.9 degree steering head angle and 22 mm clamp offset for the 2022 450 SX-F, with a 1,485 mm wheelbase, 950-960 mm seat height and 100.5 kg weight without fuel.

source.name: Total Motorcycle 2022 KTM 450 SX-F spec reprint; Dirt Bike Magazine 2022 spec sheet

records.notes: Secondary reprints of the KTM spec sheet; wheelbase from the magazine spec sheet. Head angle is the same 63.9 deg KTM lists for 2023-2026, so the 2023 frame did not change the published head angle. KTM does not publish trail.

records.topic: aftermarket adjustable-offset clamps and stock clamp weight
records.statement: Every KTM, Husqvarna and GasGas motocross bike since 2016 (GasGas since 2021) uses 22 mm clamp offset. One aftermarket set adjusts to 21, 22, 23 or 24 mm and weighs 2,140 g with bar mounts, against 2,229 g for the stock 2026 clamps and 2,300 g for the factory split clamps.

values.older_bike_note: 2016-2022 KTM/Husqvarna and 2021-2023 GasGas need the 2023+ top bearing seal A46001086000

source.name: Luxon MX Gen3 Pro triple clamps product page

records.notes: Vendor data, including claimed adjustable stiffness (optional lower brace). Weights are the vendor's own scale figures.

records.topic: stock clamp feel: CNC vs cast/forged
records.statement: Testers find the KTM's machined clamps a little too rigid, while the GasGas uses cheaper non-machined clamps that flex more and pass more feedback to the bars: some call that forgiving, others say it sends more chatter than needed.

values.gasgas_2022: cast clamps, more flex and feedback
values.gasgas_2026: cast clamp and bars transmit more feedback than needed

source.name: Vital MX 2022 450 and 250 Shootouts; Dirt Bike Magazine 2026 450 MX Shootout

records.notes: Rider impressions. Sources disagree on whether the GasGas clamps are cast or forged (see conflicts). Applies to the 450 and 250F.

records.topic: clamp swap tests on the KX450X
records.statement: On the KX450X, the stock clamps felt soft and vague on corner entry. A stiffer upper clamp on the stock lower felt most precise without harshness. A 23 mm set steered sharply but was harsh in braking bumps. A 22 mm flexible set turned easily but felt nervous on fast ground and in sand.

values.23mm_aftermarket: very precise but harsh over chop
values.22mm_aftermarket: nimble, unsettled in sand / high speed

source.name: Dirt Bike Test: Tuned Kawasaki KX450X triple clamp testing

records.notes: Model year not stated in the text; images suggest 2023. Off-road (West Coast) use with stiffer suspension. Stock offset not stated in article.

records.statement: Fitting the stock 2024 KX250 clamps (23 mm offset, different flex) to a 2024 KX450 made the front feel lower and more planted in corners and better over square edges while leaned over, but busier on fast choppy tracks. Running the fork flush in the clamps rebalanced it.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested: Stock 2024 KX250 triple clamps on a 2024 KX450

records.notes: KX450 stock offset not stated in this article. Tester also said the 2024 KX450 generally needs stiffer settings than the 2023.

records.topic: 24 mm offset clamps on the CRF450R
records.statement: On 2020-2023 CRF450Rs the stock 22 mm offset can feel twitchy and oversteer; a 24 mm setting gave more control into corners, better lean-angle stability and less deflection in ruts.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested: Talon Raptor clamps review (Honda CRF450R)

records.notes: Single aftermarket product with insert-adjustable offset.

records.statement: One race build used offset headset cups to lay the fork out 20 minutes (0.3 degree) for a longer wheelbase and more stability, together with aftermarket engine mounts for bump compliance and lean-angle front feel.

values.fork_height_limit: no more than 5 mm up (more caused headshake and oversteer)

records.notes: Modified bike with linkage, engine mounts, clutch kit and flywheel weight; effect of the cups alone not isolated.

records.statement: Backing several chassis bolts below KTM's torque spec on the 2025 KTMs takes some of the harsh, edgy feel out when leaned over or accelerating, for example swingarm pivot 100 to 90 Nm, top engine hanger 25 to 20 Nm and top clamp pinch bolts 17 to 15 Nm. Check these bolts every other ride.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested: 2025 KTM 250/350/450 optional torque specs

records.notes: Below OEM spec; the source warns to check bolts for backing out. Stock values as quoted in the article. Source says 2023-2025 KTMs also benefit from aftermarket clamps and engine hangers. Husqvarna/GasGas share the parts but were not named.

records.statement: Billet aluminum top engine mounts are sold for 2023-2026 KTM SX-Fs and 2023.5-2026 GasGas MC 450F; the maker claims they add torsional flex for a plusher feel and more bump absorption.

values.contents: CNC aluminum top mounts, titanium front engine-mount bolt

records.notes: Vendor claims; no stiffness numbers. A tester also listed these mounts on a 2025 YZ450F race build for bump compliance and lean-angle front feel. Medium/soft aluminum mount tests on the 2023 KTM 450 are in ktm_family_setups.json.

records.statement: The frame introduced on the 2022.5 Factory Edition and the 2023 models added a stamped gusset between the down tubes, a forged one-piece head-tube section, forged chromoly engine mounts and forged aluminum head stays, and it was stiffer and needed a longer break-in. KTM shrank the rear axle from 25 to 22 mm to put some flex back into the stiffer swingarm.

values.backbone: no longer joins shock tower; splits into parallel tubes

source.name: Motocross Action: 20 innermost secrets of the 2022 KTM 450SXF Factory Edition

records.notes: Magazine report of factory engineering details. Shared 250/450 frame. 25 mm aftermarket wheels fit with spacers. Shock shortening reported as 20 mm here (corrected from 15 mm); other records say 15 mm (see conflicts).

records.statement: For 2025 KTM cut relief holes in the shock tower, thinned the forged head-tube plates and the shock-tower-to-footpeg tubes, opened up the head stays and slimmed the linkage, all to make the chassis absorb more and kick less. The forged engine mounts stayed the same.
records.notes: Magazine report of KTM changes. Husqvarna 2025 linkage uses longer arms (lowered chassis); GasGas got a 'more flexible shock linkage' and shock-tower cut-outs (per a 2025 shootout).

records.statement: Lowering the countershaft sprocket on the 2023 frame made the chain run at a steep angle, so it wore through the swingarm buffer pad and then into the aluminum swingarm. For 2025 KTM shaved the top of the swingarm and fitted a thicker pad.

values.cause: countershaft 3 mm lower, steeper chain line
values.fix_2025: swingarm top shaved, thicker buffer pad

records.notes: On 2023-2024 bikes, check the chain slider pad often and replace it before the chain reaches the swingarm. GasGas got the new chassis for 2024, so the GasGas exposure is mainly 2024.

records.statement: In a 2022 250 test, the KTM-family steel frames gave more compliance but the KTM itself still felt fairly stiff, and the GasGas was the most forgiving at some cost to precision. The Honda felt rigid, the Yamaha's aluminum frame had good flex, and testers split on whether the Kawasaki was too rigid or too flexy in chop.
records.notes: Rider impressions. Chassis tuning tools named: clamps, torque specs, engine hangers.

records.statement: Triumph fitted new engine mounts tuned for a more refined chassis feel, a steel clutch basket, a high-capacity Exedy hub and a Belleville spring to the 2026 TF 450-X. Geometry stays 27.4 deg rake, 116 mm trail and 1,492 mm wheelbase.

values.wet_weight_claim: 108.3 kg (239.4 lb), fuel state not given

records.notes: A 2026 comparison test found the frame has about the right amount of flex and noted the upgraded mounts and clutch.

records.topic: aftermarket linkage for 2023+ KTM-family big bikes
records.statement: An aftermarket linkage for 2023-2024 KTM big bikes turns the stock fairly flat rising rate around: plusher early, firmer deep in the stroke. It needs a shock spring about 0.4 N/mm stiffer (4.0 to 4.4), gives more hard-pack corner traction and chop absorption, and fixes bottoming late in the stroke.

values.ride_height: same static; feels slightly lower on track
values.best_for: vet/novice, hard-pack; pros kept stock on soft tacky dirt

source.name: Motocross Action team tested: 2023-24 KTM Pro Circuit shock linkage

records.notes: Fitment named: 2023 KTM big bikes, 2023.5 GasGas Factory Edition, Husqvarna FC 450 Rockstar Edition, 2024 GasGas big bikes. Spring units as printed (likely kg/mm-style shorthand for 40 -> 44 N/mm).

records.statement: The newer KTM shock linkage has less friction, so testers add one or two clicks of shock compression to get the same feel.
records.notes: Same test lists shock spring 45 N/mm (175 lb and up) or 42 N/mm (under 175 lb); stock went from 48 to 45 N/mm.

records.statement: An aftermarket linkage and shock re-valve on the 2021-2022 CRF450R kept rear ride height the same but cured the stink-bug feel into corners, cut harshness on acceleration chop and kept the bike flatter over braking bumps. It runs best at 105-106 mm sag with the normal spring for the rider's weight.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested: Factory Connection linkage/shock modification (2021-2022 CRF450R)

records.notes: Maker did not disclose the rod length or rate change. Reduced but did not remove the stiff chassis feel.

records.statement: A factory-supported team tested pull rods that lowered the rear 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 mm on the 2021 CRF450R; both riders picked the 0.5 mm option for a lower rear feel and less wallow in rollers.

source.name: KroozTune: Honda CRF450R 2021 linkage tested with factory Honda Australia

records.notes: Honda's 2025 update lengthened the pull rods by 0.5 mm (see honda450.json), the same direction.

records.topic: rear axle position and chain slack (2019-2022 450 SX-F)
records.statement: On the 2019-2022 450 SX-F a tester moved the axle from about 608 mm to 595 mm from the swingarm pivot, which gave more front grip out of corners and less squat on acceleration. Being 2-3 mm off is fine, but 10 mm changes the bike's character. Chain slack worked best at 65-68 mm: 60 mm felt harsh, over 68 mm felt disconnected.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested: KTM 450 SX-F chain and axle position tips

records.notes: Stock gearing; model year not stated (article Sept 2021, so 2021/2022 bike). Measured centre of pivot bolt to centre of axle. For 2025 the same source suggests 600-606 mm (cd6 optional-torque record).

records.topic: what moving the axle back does
records.statement: Moving the rear axle back makes the shock feel softer, because the swingarm has more leverage on it, so you may need more compression. It also lengthens the wheelbase and puts more weight on the front tire, which improves high-speed stability but can slow cornering. The 2019 swingarm was 5 mm longer than before.

source.name: Motocross Action: The long and short of moving your KTM axle rearward

records.notes: Written about the 2018.5 Factory Edition and 2019 450 SX-F; the principles apply to any linkage bike.

records.statement: On the TF 250-X a 51-tooth rear sprocket pulled the axle too far forward on the stock chain, so a longer chain is needed above 50 teeth; testers settled on 49 or 50.

values.51T: axle too far forward, needs longer chain

source.name: Motocross Action race test: 2025 Triumph TF250-X

records.statement: On the 2020-2022 450 SX-F (stock 13/49) a tester's pick was 14/52, to settle the rear out of corners and over square-edge and braking bumps and smooth the 2nd-to-3rd change. The 2022 Factory Edition (13/51) went to 13/52.

records.statement: On the 2023-2025 450 SX-F (stock 13/51) one tester first tried 13/52 but it did not help 3rd gear enough. In 2023 and 2024 they ran slightly taller (13/50 or 14/50) to stay in 2nd and 3rd longer, and by 2025 they kept stock 13/51 because the long 2nd gear works, with 13/52 as an option for soft East Coast dirt.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested MX gearing guides 2023-2025

records.notes: 2023 guide https://www.keeferinctesting.com/2023-mx-gearing-spec-guide/; 2024 guide https://www.keeferinctesting.com/2024-mx-gearing-guide/ lists stock as 14/51, which disagrees with KTM's 13/51 (see conflicts). Husqvarna FC 450 got identical advice.

records.statement: The Husqvarna FC 450 gets the same gearing as the KTM: 14/52 instead of stock 13/49 on 2020-2022 bikes, then 13/50 in 2023-2024 and stock 13/51 in 2025 (13/52 for soft dirt).

records.statement: On the GasGas MC 450F a tester's pick every year has been 14/52, to calm the rear out of corners and smooth the 2nd-to-3rd shift on exits.

records.notes: The guides list stock as 13/49 for every year including 2024-2025 on the new chassis; BAK should confirm stock from the GasGas manual.

records.statement: On the 250 SX-F (stock 14/51) a tester's pick is one tooth up to 14/52 for better 3rd-gear drive out of corners in soft dirt, with little loss in 2nd. They keep stock on hard pack. In 2020 they went two teeth up to 14/53.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested / PulpMX MX gearing guides 2020-2025

records.notes: Husqvarna FC 250 and GasGas MC 250F got 14/52 too.

records.statement: The Husqvarna FC 250 and GasGas MC 250F go one tooth up, from stock 14/51 to 14/52, to settle the rear end and help the 2nd-to-3rd shift on corner exits. Testers keep stock on hard pack.

records.notes: GasGas MC 250F stock listed as 14/51 in these guides; another file records a 52T stock rear for 2024-2025 (see conflicts).

records.statement: On the 350s a tester went from 14/51 to 14/53 on the 2020-2022 KTM, or 14/52 on the Husqvarna, and keeps the 2023-2025 KTM and Husqvarna at stock 14/52. The GasGas MC 350F (listed 14/51) goes to 14/52.

records.notes: No reason given for keeping 2023+ stock.

records.statement: On the TF 250-X (stock 13/48) testers go to 13/49 for better 3rd-gear recovery, so 3rd can be used earlier or held longer. Novices like 13/50.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested 2025 MX gearing guide; Motocross Action 2025 TF250-X race test

records.notes: Two sources agree on 49T for faster riders.

records.statement: On the TF 450-RC (stock 48T rear) testers fitted a 49 with a longer chain for fast and heavier (about 195 lb) riders to close the 2nd-to-3rd gap, and a 50 for riding at 8,000 ft altitude.

source.name: Dirt Bike Test: 20-hour test Triumph TF450-RC

records.notes: Altitude cuts power, so lower gearing makes up for it.

records.statement: On 2020-2022 YZ450Fs (stock 13/49) a tester's alternative is 14/53, which settles the chassis on acceleration, calms it on deceleration and keeps 3rd usable on most tracks.

records.notes: Paired with Power Tuner maps in the source.

records.statement: On 2023-2025 YZ450Fs (stock 13/49) a tester runs 13/50 on deep East Coast dirt to recover 2nd and get into 3rd sooner. They suggest 14/52 for a smoother roll-on and less chain bind under load, and stock for West Coast hard pack. Another builder chose the opposite: 14/52 in the West and 13/49 in the East.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested MX gearing guides 2023-2025; PulpMX Final Draft 2025 YZ450F

records.notes: See conflicts for the opposite East/West preference.

records.statement: On 2020-2023 YZ250Fs a tester keeps stock 13/50 and adjusts power with the ECU map instead.

records.notes: 2021 guide lists 13/50 and 13/51 as stock. 2024-2025 13/49 advice is already in yamaha_250f_2t.json.

records.statement: A tester ran 14/52 on the 2020 CRF450R to free up the rear over bumps. On 2021 and later CRF450Rs they stay with a 13T countershaft sprocket, because a 14T sits too close to the hydraulic clutch slave cylinder: 13/49 stock, 13/50 in 2024-2025 to help it pull in a higher gear.

values.2021_2022: 13/49 stock (14T too close to slave cylinder)

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested / PulpMX MX gearing guides 2020-2025

records.notes: The slave-cylinder clearance problem on 2021+ bikes is the key fact: avoid 14T fronts.

records.statement: On 2020-2021 CRF250Rs (stock 13/48) a tester went to 13/49 or 13/50 because 2nd and 3rd felt too close. On 2022-2025 bikes (stock 13/50) they run 13/51 to get into 3rd earlier, with stock fine on flowing tracks. The 2025 Works Edition stays at 13/50 unless the rider weighs over 190 lb.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested / PulpMX MX gearing guides 2020-2025

records.statement: On the KX450 (stock 13/50) a tester usually runs 13/51 so 3rd pulls out of corners without heavy clutch use. On the 2024 they kept stock because 13/51 did not help bottom end and shortened the useful long 2nd gear, then went back to 13/51 in 2025.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested / PulpMX MX gearing guides 2020-2025

records.notes: See conflicts for 2024 vs 2025.

records.statement: On the KX250 (stock 13/50) a tester kept stock through 2022, then ran 13/51 from 2023 for 3rd-gear roll-on. On the 2025, the new airbox costs some bottom-end pickup, and the extra tooth gets back into the power sooner.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested / PulpMX MX gearing guides 2020-2025

records.statement: Race teams usually add one rear tooth for sand (for example 50 to 51) so the engine pulls out of deep corners, and accept a little more shifting. They also add a few clicks of compression for the bigger sand bumps.

values.tires: hard-pack front with sand rear if the base is hard

source.name: Racer X: The Breakdown: Walker on Sand

records.notes: General team practice, not model-specific; older article. A 2022 technical article agrees: deep sand or disced dirt calls for an extra rear tooth. A 2019 forum thread on a 250 two-stroke showed no agreement (one rider went taller to 48T to hold 3rd), so it depends on the bike's power.

records.statement: One technical column suggests 1-2 extra rear teeth for supercross-style tracks (stock 50 to 51-52 on a KX450) for instant acceleration, one tooth less (49) for wide-open motocross tracks, and 2-3 fewer (47-48) or a 14T front for desert. Hard pack can like taller gearing because a softer hit spins the tire less.

source.name: Dirt Bike Magazine: Gearing 101 (Mr. Know-It-All); Motocross Action Tech Spec on sprockets

records.notes: Worked example was a 2025 KX450 (13/50); the logic is general. Bigger rear sprockets may need a longer chain. Arenacross-specific numbers not found.

records.statement: KTM says its factory supercross bikes are geared differently from motocross bikes, use firmer and more rigid suspension settings with the same hardware, and run stronger rims and hubs for big jumps.

source.name: KTM: From the deepest rut to the stadium floor

records.notes: Qualitative only; no sprocket numbers published.

records.topic: gear ratio comparison of common sprocket combos

values.front_tooth_equivalent: one front tooth = rear teeth / 14, about 3.5 (49T) to 3.7 (52T) rear teeth

records.notes: Ratio = rear teeth / front teeth. Going from 13 to 14 front at rear R gives ratio R/14; the same ratio on a 13 front needs 13R/14 rear teeth, so the step is R/14 teeth (49/14 = 3.5; 51/14 = 3.64; 52/14 = 3.71). Magazines quote 'about 3' (one) or '2.5-3' (another); the true figure at MX gearing is about 3.5-3.7. 13/51 -> 14/52: 3.923 / 3.714 = 1.056, so 5.3% taller.

records.statement: Testers often move to a 14T countershaft with a bigger rear sprocket (e.g. 14/52 instead of 13/49) because it settles the rear on acceleration and braking bumps. One rider reports a smaller countershaft adds squat and makes the bike easier to loft or seat-bounce. Small countershafts also wear chains faster, so going one tooth bigger in front and about three bigger at the back is common.

values.tester_choice: 14T front + bigger rear to calm the rear
values.small_countershaft: more squat (single rider report), faster chain wear
values.chain: bigger combo needs a longer chain

source.name: Vital MX forum: Help settle a sprocket debate; Motocross Action gearing article

records.notes: The squat effect comes from one poster; most posters said the chain-wear difference is small. Do not use 14T on 2021+ CRF450R (slave cylinder clearance). KTM lowered its countershaft 3 mm in 2023 for the same anti-squat reason.

records.statement: The KTM and Husqvarna 450s have the most robust clutch in the class, with a one-piece machined steel basket and machined-in primary gear, and the factory teams race the stock clutch. The GasGas uses cheaper BrakTec hydraulics; they improved for 2025 but still rate below the Brembo parts.

values.ktm_husqvarna_basket: one-piece CNC steel, machined-in primary gear

records.notes: Another 2025 test rated the Husqvarna's Brembo clutch best in class (Cycle News).

records.statement: Testers called the 2021-2022 KTM-family hydraulic clutches a little on/off or vague in feel. Husqvarna used Magura parts then, and at least one tester preferred them to KTM's Brembo. Most rated Kawasaki's hydraulic clutch the best feeling.
records.notes: Rider impressions. Husqvarna switched to Brembo for 2025 (ktm350f.json).

records.statement: KTM's heavier '280' Belleville clutch spring (part 78932005000) comes stock on Factory Edition 450 SX-Fs since 2013 and is a common way to stop slip. Check the hub rubber dampers every 20 hours on SX-F models.
records.notes: Fitment of the 280 spring to 2023+ engines not confirmed by this source; check the KTM parts catalog. The stiffer spring increases lever effort.

records.statement: A thin-plate friction pack (more discs in the stock basket) is sold for 2013-2026 KTM 450 SX-Fs with a claimed 25% more torque capacity and 10% lighter pull. A complete kit with a steel-pin hub, billet pressure plate and cover is sold for 2023+ 250/350 SX-F and FC models.

source.name: Rekluse product pages and dealer listings

records.notes: Vendor claims, no independent test found for the KTM fitment. Rekluse auto-clutch setup: 3-6 mm free-play gain at about 5,000 rpm, no 3rd-gear starts during break-in. Fitment tables on vendor pages are inconsistent; confirm by part number. Dealer listing: https://motohousemx.com/products/rekluse-racing-torqdrive-clutch-pack-2013-2020-ktm-450-sx-f-rms-2813086

records.topic: clutch slip and drag causes (owner reports)
records.statement: Owners with slipping or dragging KTM clutches point to a few causes: Belleville spring set flatter than the factory position (burnt plates), very short levers, worn hub rubber dampers and warped pressure plates. No single cause was agreed.

values.spring_setting: factory position 2 worked; flat burnt plates

source.name: Vital MX forum: KTM clutch observation/issue

records.notes: Thread covered a 2019 450 SX-F plus other KTMs; about 15 posters, no consensus.

records.topic: TF 250-X clutch fix and basket design
records.statement: Triumph issued a free fix for 2024 TF 250-X clutches: a new basket with oil and heat holes, new fiber plates and a new clutch sensor. The 250's basket is aluminum with a riveted primary gear, while the 2025 TF 450-RC uses a steel basket.

values.fix_2024: new basket with oil/heat holes, new fiber plates, new clutch sensor

source.name: Motocross Action race test: 2025 Triumph TF250-X

records.notes: Magazine report of the Triumph fix; testers had no failures but knew riders who broke plates. On the 450-RC a 20-hour test found engagement a little long, and a Hinson kit added bite (kit already in triumph_gapfill.json).

records.statement: The 2024-2026 KX450 clutch fades with light abuse and its engagement can drift mid-moto, partly because the steel plates notch the aluminum hub. A five-coil-spring replacement clutch and a steel-pin-hub kit both gave consistent engagement with no fade in deep sand.

source.name: Keefer Inc. Tested: Hinson small diameter clutch and Rekluse APEX reviews (2024-2026 KX450)

records.statement: Testers found the 2025 CRF450R hydraulic clutch inconsistent on starts; some riders fit a Kawasaki Nissin master cylinder to fix it.
records.notes: A 2026 test instead called the Honda clutch great; the 2026 change may matter.

records.statement: A CRF450R owner chasing a 'clutch' that would not drive found the countershaft and sprocket splines ground off; aftermarket sprockets of different thickness can stop the cup washer clamping the sprocket.
